_notes: Her window is dark, and her window is never dark. Two ways home, the empty hall, and the climb in through the workroom window.
Scenes 18-25 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

lines: Old green shutters that fold back against the brick, folded back every evening of my life: in rain, in frost, in the week the chimney caught. She did not close them for weather. She did not close them.
Something in me tried to file that and could not find the drawer. So I told myself she was out.
Two ways home. The long way passes the Lamplighters' hall, where whatever silenced the lamps went wrong first — eleven minutes, perhaps twelve.
The fast way is over the fences, and the fences are a young cat's road.
choices: The long way — see what silenced the lamps
scenes.art_desc: Deep in the fogged lane at night, every street lamp dark, one lamplighter's ladder still leaning against an unlit lamp
Lamplighters' guild hall interior, abandoned mid-shift: racked ladders, cold kettle, one silver thread glinting on a lamp-hook
lines: I took the long way, and I have had a long time to decide why. The wrongness at the head of the route. Her voice saying look before you leap. A breath already taken off me once tonight. All three are true; I have not decided.

The hall stood open, ladders racked, coats on their pegs, and the kettle on the little stove cold — and a guild hall's kettle is never cold. Forty men and women walk out of this room every evening and light a city. Nobody was in it.
Caught on a lamp-hook by the door: a thread of silver. HER stitching. I would know it under floodwater. Why was she HERE?
notes: ❋ Her Stitching joins your deck — a Moonlight 2, and the only card of its kind you own.

lines: Out of the hall and eleven streets home, and I do not remember eight of them.
Her street. Her gate. Her drainpipe, the one I have used nine hundred times, and up — slower than nine hundred times, my back legs arguing the whole way.

scenes.art_desc: Ash in full sprint leaping between fence tops at night, fog blurred with speed, a dark window ahead
lines: Over the fences, and I pay for every one of them. The hall goes by dark on my left. Later, if there is a later.
Up the drainpipe I have used nine hundred times, and in. Fast enough that something inside is still busy.
In through the workroom window. The house is doing the wrong thing with sound: a kettle screaming, and nobody going to it.
The workroom is wrong. Forty years of her work hung like a garden on the walls, cut — every thread snipped at the same height, cleanly, as if by someone tidying.
The parlor door stands open and I do not go through it. Not yet. I stop at the threshold, low, and I look.

scenes.art_desc: The Unpicked: a person-shaped absence woven from the room's own unravelled threads, standing in a doorway
lines: Something is standing in the parlor doorway, wearing the room. It is person-shaped the way a coat on a hook is person-shaped, and it is made of HER threads — pulled out of the walls and put ON.
It looked at me, decided I was not an interruption, and went back to its work. That is the part I will keep. Every hair I have is standing up. Good. Let them.
